hook_text: Some rivers near old South African mines run orange. The reason is a mineral called fool's gold.
clip_script: Gold built Johannesburg. Coal makes most of our electricity. Platinum from the Bushveld cleans car exhaust around the world. Mining gives jobs to hundreds of thousands of people. But there is a cost. Deep in many mines is pyrite, fool's gold. Mining exposes it to air and water, and it makes sulfuric acid. The acid dissolves toxic metals and turns the water orange. When old mines flood, that acid water overflows into rivers and can keep flowing for decades, killing fish and poisoning water. Add dust from mine dumps and the lung disease silicosis, and you see why the law now says: study the impacts first, control them while mining, and fix the land afterwards. In eMalahleni, mine water is even cleaned into drinking water.
visual_style: Aerial shots of mine dumps and open pits; an orange stream beside a green one; a pyrite crystal glinting; a water treatment plant turning orange water clear.
pacing: Proud open on mineral wealth, a sharp turn to the hidden cost, a hopeful close on solutions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out how you can help reduce the need for new mining.
